name: Magnesium
mobility: MOBILE in plant (deficiency on OLD leaves first)

overview.whyImportant: Magnesium is the CENTRAL ATOM of the chlorophyll molecule — no Mg, no green, no photosynthesis. It also activates many enzymes and helps move phosphorus. Deficiency shows as classic interveinal yellowing of older leaves with green veins.

plantFunctions.roleInsidePlant: Central atom of chlorophyll; enzyme activator; P carrier.
plantFunctions.rootDevelopment: Supports energy transfer for root growth.
plantFunctions.vegetativeGrowth: Maintains green leaf area and photosynthesis.
plantFunctions.proteinSynthesis: Needed for ribosome function and protein synthesis.
plantFunctions.enzymeActivation: Activates ATPases and many phosphate-transfer enzymes.
plantFunctions.yieldContribution: Sustains photosynthesis and sugar loading; deficiency cuts yield and quality.

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Usually adequate, but high Ca can antagonise Mg.
Acid sandy soils are genuinely low in Mg; leaching.

whyDeficiencyHappens.condition: Nutrient imbalance / excess K, Ca, NH4
whyDeficiencyHappens.why: These cations strongly antagonise Mg uptake — heavy MOP is a classic trigger.
High K blocks Mg uptake — the most common induced Mg deficiency.
Heavy K without Mg; ignoring Mg on sandy/acid soils.

symptoms.note: Mg is MOBILE — deficiency on OLD leaves first. Signature: interveinal yellowing with GREEN VEINS (Christmas-tree pattern).
symptoms.early: Older leaves show interveinal yellowing while veins stay green.
symptoms.middle: Pronounced interveinal chlorosis, sometimes reddish/purple tints, on older leaves.
symptoms.severe: Interveinal areas turn brown/necrotic, older leaves die; reduced photosynthesis and yield.
symptoms.oldLeaves: First affected: yellow between veins, green veins remain (net-like/Christmas-tree look).
symptoms.wholePlant: Lower leaves netted-yellow moving up, reduced vigour and yield.

cropWiseSymptoms.symptoms: Interveinal yellowing/orange of older leaves on sandy/acid soils.
Interveinal chlorosis of older leaves, green veins, on light soils.
Older-leaf interveinal yellowing on sandy soils.
Older-leaf interveinal yellowing, especially after heavy K fertigation.
Classic interveinal chlorosis of older leaves in high-K fertigation (induced Mg deficiency).
Interveinal yellowing of outer older leaves.
Strong interveinal chlorosis of older leaves (green veins), common in heavy-fruiting fertigated vines.
Interveinal striping/yellowing of older leaves, reddish-purple tints in severe cases.
Interveinal chlorosis of older leaves on sandy soils.
Older-leaf interveinal chlorosis on light soils.
Interveinal yellowing/rusty older leaves on sandy/acid soils, reduced vigour.

howToFix.methodOfApplication: Foliar for fast correction; soil/fertigation for sustained supply
Broadcast + incorporate; corrects acidity + supplies Mg & Ca
howToFix.precautions: Best long-term fix for acid sandy soils low in Mg.

methodOfApplication.broadcast: MgSO4 or dolomite broadcast + incorporate for soil correction.
methodOfApplication.foliarSpray: 1-2% MgSO4 for fast greening of interveinal chlorosis.

toxicity.whatHappens: Mg toxicity is rare; excess Mg antagonises Ca and K uptake and can worsen soil structure (as in serpentine soils).
toxicity.correctionMethods: Balance with Ca/K; avoid excess dolomite.

prevention: Use dolomite on acid sandy soils to supply Mg long-term.
Don't over-apply K/MOP without Mg — the main induced-deficiency cause.
Include MgSO4 in fertigation schedules for heavy-fruiting veg.
Maintain K:Mg balance via soil test.
Build organic matter for Mg retention.
On sandy soils apply Mg regularly.
Foliar MgSO4 preventively in high-K crops (cucumber/capsicum).
Correct acidity to improve Mg availability.
Monitor older leaves for early interveinal signs.
commonFarmerMistakes: Heavy MOP/K fertigation with no Mg — induces Mg deficiency.
Confusing Mg interveinal chlorosis (old leaves) with Fe (young leaves).
Ignoring Mg on acid sandy soils.
Not using dolomite when both Ca and Mg are low.
Over-liming with pure calcitic lime, worsening Mg imbalance.
Foliar MgSO4 too strong (>2%) causing scorch.
Treating Mg chlorosis as a disease.
Skipping soil test for K:Mg ratio.
Not correcting the K excess that caused it.
Ignoring Mg in high-yield fruit crops that remove a lot.
Assuming NPK blends cover Mg (most don't).
Not splitting Mg on sandy soils.
Waiting until severe necrosis to act.
expertTips: Diagnose Mg by OLD-leaf interveinal yellowing with GREEN VEINS (vs Fe on young leaves).
Use dolomite for a long-term Mg + Ca + pH fix on acid sandy soils.
After heavy K fertigation, add MgSO4 to prevent induced deficiency.
Foliar 1-2% MgSO4 gives fast greening in 7-10 days.
Keep the K:Mg ratio balanced (soil test).
Include Mg routinely in cucumber/capsicum/tomato fertigation.
Epsom salt (MgSO4) is cheap, soluble, and doubles as sulphur.
On sandy soils, apply Mg every season.
Don't over-lime with calcitic lime where Mg is low — use dolomite.
Ensure moisture at Mg application.
Split Mg on leaching-prone soils.
Watch older leaves at heavy-fruiting stage for early Mg signs.
Balance Mg with Ca to avoid mutual antagonism.
Use Mg-nitrate for clean fertigation solubility.
Correct soil acidity to free up native Mg.
Combine soil Mg (sustained) with foliar Mg (fast) for stubborn cases.
High-yield sugar/fruit crops need planned Mg.
Avoid tank-mixing MgSO4 with high-Ca products in hard water (haze).

faq.q: Purani patti nason ke beech pili, nasein hari — kya?
faq.a: Magnesium ki kami. 1-2% MgSO4 (Epsom salt) chhidkein; acid sandy mitti me dolomite dein.

faq.q: Mg aur Fe deficiency me farak?
faq.a: Mg = purani (neeche) patti; Fe = nayi (upar) patti. Dono interveinal, par patti ki umar se pehchaan.

faq.q: Zyada MOP se Mg kami hoti hai?
faq.a: Haan — zyada K, Mg uptake block karta hai. MgSO4 add karein aur K balance rakhein.
1-2% (10-20 g/L); isse zyada nahi warna patti jal sakti hai.
Acid sandy mitti me jahan Ca aur Mg dono kam hon — pH bhi sudhrega.

faq.q: Cucumber/capsicum me Mg kami kyun common?
faq.a: Bhaari fruiting + high-K fertigation se induced Mg deficiency. Fertigation me MgSO4 shaamil karein.

faq.q: Mg ka asar kitne din me?
faq.a: Foliar 7-10 din me hariyali.
Magnesium sulphate — sasta, ghulnsheel, Mg + sulphur dono deta hai.
Har season thodi maatra, ya dolomite — kyunki Mg leach ho jata hai.

faq.q: NPK blend me Mg hota hai?
faq.a: Zyadatar me nahi — alag se Mg dena padta hai.
Nahi — nutrient disorder; symmetric, purani patti par. Fungicide bekaar.
Ca/K uptake block ho sakta hai — balance rakhein.
Foliar fast, soil sustained — zid problem me dono.
Severe Mg deficiency ho sakti hai; MgSO4 dein, soil test karein.
Clean fertigation ke liye polyhouse/veg me.
Zyada K, Mg rok deta hai — soil test se balance rakhein.
Dolomite se — acidity theek + Mg supply.

faq.q: Kya Mg se meethas badhti hai?
faq.a: Indirect — photosynthesis/sugar loading sudharta hai to quality behtar.
Heavy fruiting stage par purani patti dekhein.
High-Ca products ke saath mix na karein (haze/jam).
